draft.title: Exponential functions
card: An exponential function has the form y = aˣ, where the base a is a positive number and a ≠ 1. The variable x is the power.
the graph rises from left to right. It is growth: y gets bigger as x increases, and y gets closer to 0 as x becomes very negative.
the graph falls from left to right. It is decay: y gets smaller as x increases, and y gets very large as x becomes very negative.

Both graphs pass through (0, 1), because a⁰ = 1. Both stay above the x-axis and get closer to the line y = 0 on one side without touching it. This line is the horizontal asymptote. Example: y = 2ˣ has points (0, 1), (1, 2) and (3, 8).
draft.remember: Every y = aˣ passes through (0, 1), stays above the x-axis and has y = 0 as its asymptote.

a.q: Which statement is true for the graph of y = (1/2)ˣ?
opts: It falls from left to right and passes through (0, 1)
It rises from left to right and passes through (0, 1)
It falls from left to right and passes through (0, 0)
It rises from left to right and passes through (1, 0)
a.why: The base 1/2 is between 0 and 1, so the graph falls. Any base to the power 0 is 1, so it passes through (0, 1). Through (0, 0) is wrong because aˣ is never 0.
a.clue: Is the base more than 1 or between 0 and 1? What is a⁰?

b.q: Mia graphs y = 3ˣ and y = (1/3)ˣ on the same axes. Which statement is true for both graphs?
opts: Both have the horizontal asymptote y = 0
Both rise from left to right
Both cross the x-axis at x = 1
b.why: Both have positive bases not equal to 1, so both have y-intercept 1 and get closer to y = 0 without touching it. The graph of y = 3ˣ rises but y = (1/3)ˣ falls, so rising is not true for both.
b.clue: Think about what both graphs share, whatever the base.

a.best: It falls from left to right and passes through (0, 1)

b.best: Both have the horizontal asymptote y = 0
